hpi: Differential: Group A Streptococcal Pharyngitis, Retropharyngeal abscess, Epiglottitis, Lemierre Syndrome, Lateral Pharyngeal Abscess, Other Bacterial pharyngitis. This patient has viral pharyngitis. The exact virus will not be determined in the case as it typically is not determined in real life. The main point of the case is to not over-treat. It is important to rule out a Group A Streptococcal infection by doing a rapid group A strep test. If negative, give only symptomatic relief with pain medications (ibuprofen or Acetaminophen) along with salt water gargles which has been shown to help. No other interventions are necessary in this case. In time, the patient will begin to feel better. If you give antibiotics, you would fail the case. Antibiotics can cause harm in viral infections do not help and have led to antibiotic resistance.
